description: A flexible authorization library that combines role-based (RBAC), attribute-based (ABAC), and relationship-based (ReBAC) access control policies.

summary.one_liner: Gatehouse is an in-process Rust authorization engine that combines RBAC, ABAC-style predicates, and relationship-based (ReBAC) policies, with request-scoped fact loading for list endpoints.
summary.what_it_does: Lets applications define typed authorization domains (subject, action, resource, context) and register grant policies and veto policies with a PermissionChecker. Policies can be synchronous predicates built with PolicyBuilder, async Policy/VetoPolicy implementations, built-in RbacPolicy and RebacPolicy, or DelegatingPolicy that maps inputs into another domain. Each request gets an EvaluationSession that batches, deduplicates, caches, and coalesces fact loads from registered FactSource implementations. Evaluation returns Granted, Denied, or Indeterminate decisions with audit traces, and list helpers (try_filter, try_lookup_page) authorize already-loaded resources or enumerate candidate IDs via LookupSource and Hydrator. Deny-overrides semantics keep veto authority separate from grants.
use_cases: authorize access to a single resource in a Rust web service
filter list endpoint results by user permissions
relationship-based checks such as document owner or viewer via SQL facts
role-based access control in Rust applications
deny-override global bans or account suspension rules
paginated authorized lists using lookup and hydration
how_to_run: Add to Cargo.toml: gatehouse = "=0.6.0-alpha.3" and tokio = { version = "1", features = ["macros", "rt"] }
Replace src/main.rs with the quickstart program from the README
notable: Deny-overrides veto model: definite vetoes deny, uncertainty blocks grants, and any independent grant authorizes
EvaluationSession batches, deduplicates, caches, and coalesces fact loads per request, targeting N+1 query problems
Strict list filtering (try_filter) fails on authorization outages instead of silently omitting items
Evaluation traces and fact provenance for audit, with optional serde serialization
Must-use result types that warn when decisions are discarded
caveats: Pre-release version (0.6.0-alpha.3) pinned in the quickstart; migration guide from 0.5 is referenced as MIGRATION.md
authorize does not lock resources or provide transactional guarantees; version checks are the caller's responsibility
EvaluationSession caches are per-pass, so long-lived streams need periodic reauthorization with fresh sessions
